input: grid is a rectangular R by C binary integer array, with 1 for land and 0 for water. Empty outer arrays and zero-column rows are supported. Total R * C is within the shared collection-size bound. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. Python integers are plain int values, excluding bool; node identity keys, when used, are opaque id values.
return: Nonnegative integer number of land cells with no cardinal land-only path to any boundary cell. Empty grids return zero.
mutation_aliasing: Sets exactly boundary-connected land cells to zero in the existing grid rows. Grid and row identities remain unchanged; enclave land cells remain one. Traversal private queue/visited storage does not escape.
numeric: Coordinate and result arithmetic is bounded by R * C; every boundary cell is seeded once by the nested index loop, including one-row/one-column grids. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(R * C + R + 1) time and O(R * C + R + 1) auxiliary space. Every land cell is enqueued at most once, marked on enqueue. Queue uses a head cursor; processed entries remain allocated and are included in the space bound. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.
